mentor.name: Mémé Truelle
mentor.hello: Welcome to the site. I'm Mémé Truelle, forty years on building sites. We'll go one step at a time.
mentor.notYet: Not yet. I don't see it on GitHub. Did it go?
mentor.connectGithub: To do it for real, the site office needs your GitHub key: run gh auth login, then reload.

rankDone.apprentice: That's the Apprentice rank. You know your way around now.
rankDone.journeyman: That's the Journeyman rank. Your first contribution is in, from branch to merge. Real projects are next.
rankDone.team-leader: That's the Team leader rank. You know git from end to end. Real projects are waiting for you.
rankDone.real-project: That's the whole path. You know GitHub from the first issue to a real project. Welcome to the crew.
rankDone.site-foreman: That's the Site foreman rank. What comes in is sorted, ready and sized. Planning is next.
rankDone.site-manager: That's the Site manager rank. The week is planned, the visit is set, big jobs are cut and roped. Steering is next.
rankDone.project-director: That's the Project director rank, and the whole lead's path. You can run a site from the first parcel to the mayor's visit.

mentor.noGoodFirst: No issue is marked "good first issue" on this project yet. Ask its team, or come back later.

choose.question: Are you here to lend a hand, or to run the site?

mentor.boardCatchingUp: GitHub is still putting the parcels on your board: it can take a minute. Reload the site in a moment.

sprint.rule: The game's rule, not GitHub's: say how many points the team can carry this week. Each size counts {{points}}.
sprint.refused: A capacity is a whole number from 1 to 100.

mentor.noVisit: No visit is open: reopen the milestone on GitHub, or ask the mayor for a new one.
mentor.duplicateReason: The duplicate is closed, but not as a duplicate: reopen it on GitHub, then close it as a duplicate of the original.
mentor.selected: Selected: copy it with your keys
mentor.pullClosed: Pull request #{{number}} was closed without merging: reopen it on GitHub, or open a new one from your branch. The clean-up comes after the merge.

a1-walk.goal: Walk with the keys or the arrows, then open a pallet.
a1-walk.lesson: First, look around. Each crate on a pallet is a piece of work. Go and open one.
a1-walk.done: There. You can walk and look. That's half the job.

a2-read-issue.goal: Read the open card: its title, its text, its labels. Then press "Got it, Mémé".
a2-read-issue.lesson: That's an issue. A job written down so nobody forgets it. Read the title first, always.
a2-read-issue.done: Title, text, labels. You read it like a pro.

a3-read-board.goal: Push a pallet to another yard and confirm.
a3-read-board.lesson: Each fenced yard is a column of the board. When a pallet moves on, the work moves on. Push one, you'll see.
a3-read-board.done: See? The pallet moved, the work moved. That's all a board is.

a4-found-site.goal: Create your practice site: a repository and its board, in your own GitHub account.
a4-found-site.lesson: Enough of the pretend site. You get your own, in your own account. Nobody else's work is at risk there.
a4-found-site.done: Your own site. Your name on the gate.

a5-write-issue.goal: Write your first issue on your site: a clear title, a few words of text.
a5-write-issue.lesson: A good issue says what to do and why, with a title anyone understands. Short is fine.
a5-write-issue.done: Your first issue. Written down, nobody forgets it.

a6-take-issue.goal: Take your issue: assign yourself and say so in a comment.
a6-take-issue.lesson: When you take a job, say it out loud. Then everyone knows it's yours.
a6-take-issue.done: You said "I'll take it". Now everyone knows it's yours. Nobody else will do it twice.

a7-move-issue.goal: Push your issue out of the first column of your board.
a7-move-issue.lesson: Work you've started belongs in the next column. The board must say what's true.
a7-move-issue.done: Moving on. Your board tells the truth.

a8-edit-file.goal: With the trowel, change your README: say what your site is. The game puts it on a branch of its own.
a8-edit-file.lesson: A branch is a copy you can mess up safely. Main stays clean until your work is checked.
a8-edit-file.done: Your first commit. Signed, dated, kept forever.

a9-open-pull.goal: Open a pull request from your branch. The game adds "Closes #N" so your issue closes with it.
a9-open-pull.lesson: A pull request is you knocking on the door: "I've done this, can you look?"
a9-open-pull.done: Door knocked. Now someone can look at your work before it goes in.

a10-answer-review.goal: Do what the inspector asks, then send your change again on the same branch.
a10-answer-review.lesson: A review is not a telling-off. It's a second pair of eyes. You answer with a new commit, not a new pull request.
a10-answer-review.done: Fixed and sent. The pull request took your new commit by itself.

a11-merge.goal: Merge your pull request. Your issue closes and your first floor goes up.
a11-merge.lesson: Merging is laying the floor for real: your work joins main, and the issue it closes is done.
a11-merge.done: There it is, your first floor. You're a journeyman now.

a12-push-branch.goal: On your machine: clone your site, make a branch, change the README, commit, push. The commands are below.
a12-push-branch.lesson: Now the real tools. Everything you did with the trowel, git does on your machine. GitHub only sees it when you push.
a12-push-branch.done: Your branch came all the way from your machine. That's how the pros work.

a13-bring-main.goal: The mayor changed the plan on main. Bring main into your branch on your machine, then push.
a13-bring-main.lesson: Others keep working while you do. Before you hand in, take their latest work into yours, so nothing clashes later.
a13-bring-main.done: Up to date with main. No surprise at the merge.

a14-fix-from-machine.skill: Fix a pull request from your machine
a14-fix-from-machine.goal: Open the pull request from your branch, then push a fix from your machine: a new commit on the same branch.
a14-fix-from-machine.lesson: Same as with the trowel: the pull request follows your branch. Push again and it updates by itself.
a14-fix-from-machine.done: Fixed from your machine. The pull request took it in.

a15-clean-up.goal: Merge your pull request, then delete your branch, on GitHub and on your machine.
a15-clean-up.lesson: A merged branch is a finished job. Sweep the site: delete it, so the next person sees only work in progress.
a15-clean-up.done: Site swept. You're a team leader now.

a16-ask-good-first.skill: Ask for a good first issue
a16-ask-good-first.goal: On the real site, open a pallet marked "good first issue" and ask for it in a comment.
a16-ask-good-first.lesson: On a real project, you don't take: you ask. Someone who runs it will say yes and assign you. That's how trust starts.
a16-ask-good-first.done: You asked like a pro. Now a maintainer decides, and you'll see your badge on the site when they say yes.

l1-found-team.goal: Found your team site: a repository and its board, with the five zones and a Size field.
l1-found-team.lesson: Running a site starts with a place for the work. Five zones, from the stock to the laid floors, so anyone sees where each job stands.
l1-found-team.done: Your team site is up. Five zones, and a way to say how big each job is.

l2-sort-parcels.goal: Open the mayor's six parcels: put a label on each, and close the one that repeats another as a duplicate.
l2-sort-parcels.lesson: Here are my small ideas! Six of them. Some are clear, some are not, and one of them you have seen before.
l2-sort-parcels.done: Sorted. Every parcel has its label, and the duplicate is closed with its reason.

l3-ready.goal: On one parcel, write the checklist of what must be true before work starts, then move it to Ready to lay.
l3-ready.lesson: Nothing goes on the scaffolding until it is ready. A checklist under the issue: what to do, how we know it is done. Then, and only then, Ready to lay.
l3-ready.done: Stamped by the inspection. That one can be laid without surprises.

l4-size.goal: Give a size to every job in Ready to lay: XS, S, M, L or XL.
l4-size.lesson: A size is not a promise of time. It says how big the job looks, so you never load more than the team can carry.
l4-size.done: Every ready job has its size. Now you can plan.

l5-sprint.goal: Make a one-week sprint, say how many points the team can carry, then load the truck without going over.
l5-sprint.lesson: A sprint is a promise for one week. Load what the team can carry, not what you wish it could. The capacity is the game's rule: GitHub has none.
l5-sprint.done: The truck is loaded and it holds. That's a sprint.

l6-milestone.goal: Make a milestone with a due date, and put the jobs she wants to see under it.
l6-milestone.lesson: A milestone is a date everyone can see, and the work that must be laid by then. It tells the team what matters, and when.
l6-milestone.done: The mayor's visit is on the calendar, with what she'll see.

l7-split.goal: Cut the job far too big into smaller parts, at least two, each its own issue.
l7-split.lesson: A job too big never moves: nobody knows where to start. Cut it into parts small enough to lay in a few days. The big one becomes a building, the parts its floors.
l7-split.done: The big job is in parts now. Each can be laid on its own.

l8-rope.goal: Mark that one job waits for another: blocked by it.
l8-rope.lesson: Some jobs can't start before another is done. Saying so on the board stops anyone lifting the wrong pallet first.
l8-rope.done: The two pallets are roped. Everyone can see which goes first.

l9-bulletin.goal: Post a status update on your board: how the site stands tonight, in a few lines.
l9-bulletin.lesson: A team that knows where things stand works calmer. Say it plainly, good news or bad: on track, at risk, off track.
l9-bulletin.done: The bulletin is on the air. Everyone knows where the site stands.

l10-wip.skill: Keep work in progress under the limit
l10-wip.goal: Set a limit on Being laid, let the team's day push it over, then bring it back under.
l10-wip.lesson: Too many jobs started at once and none gets finished. A limit says: finish before you start another.
l10-wip.done: Being laid is back under its limit. Things get finished again.

l11-visit.goal: When the jobs of her visit are done, close the milestone. If they won't be, move the date and say so.
l11-visit.lesson: A date is a promise. Keep it, or move it early and openly; never let it slip in silence.
l11-visit.done: The mayor's visit is settled. That's how a project is steered.

found.title: Found your site
found.body: The game creates {{name}} in your own GitHub account, with a board to play on. Only you write there.
found.reuse: {{name}} already exists in your account: the game uses it as it is and only adds the board. Nothing in it is changed.

take.title: Take an issue
take.none: No open issue on your site yet: write one first.

summary.found: Create the repository {{owner}}/{{name}} ({{visibility}}) and its board.
summary.foundReuse: Add a board to your repository {{owner}}/{{name}}.
summary.issue: Write the issue "{{title}}" in {{repo}} and put it on your board.
summary.foundation: First, lay the foundation stone: a README as the first commit of {{repo}}.
summary.edit: Write {{path}} on the branch {{branch}}, with the message "{{message}}".
summary.pull: Open a pull request from {{branch}}, "{{title}}", which closes issue #{{number}}.
summary.merge: Merge pull request #{{number}} into the default branch of {{repo}}.
summary.mayor: Add the mayor's line to PLAN.md on {{branch}} of {{repo}}.

edit.title: Edit your README
edit.messageLabel: What you changed, in a few words
edit.foundation: Your repository is still empty: the game lays its first stone (a README) before your branch.

pull.title: Open a pull request
pull.closes: The game adds "Closes #{{number}}" at the end, so issue #{{number}} closes when this is merged.

merge.title: Merge your pull request
merge.body: Pull request #{{number}} joins your main branch, and the issue it closes is closed.

practice.blockedIssue: No open issue of yours on your site: take one first, your work happens on an issue that is yours.
practice.blockedPull: No open pull request of yours closes an issue: open one first.

mayor.open: Let the mayor change the plan
mayor.title: The mayor changes the plan
mayor.body: The mayor adds a line to PLAN.md on main. Your branch then has to catch up.

ask.title: Ask for this issue
ask.body: The game adds your comment to the issue. It assigns nobody: a maintainer decides.
ask.comment: Hello! I'd like to work on this one, if nobody has it yet. Could you assign it to me?

inspector.name: The inspector
inspector.remark: Good start. One thing: add a line saying why you made this change, then send it again. A pull request takes new commits, no need to open another one.

team-found.title: Found your team site
team-found.body: The game creates {{name}} in your account, with a board of five zones and a Size field. Only you write there.

parcels.title: The mayor's parcels
parcels.body: Six FICTIF issues arrive on your team site, each marked as written by project-quest for practice.

label.title: Label issue #{{number}}
label.body: A label says what kind of job it is, so the right people find it.

duplicate.title: Close issue #{{number}} as a duplicate
duplicate.body: It repeats another issue: close it and point to the original, so nobody does it twice.

checklist.title: Definition of Ready for issue #{{number}}
checklist.body: One line per thing that must be true before work starts. Then move it to Ready to lay.

size.title: Size issue #{{number}}
size.body: How big does it look? Not how long: how big.

summary.team-found: Set up {{repo}}: the repository and board it still needs, the five zones and the Size field.
summary.parcels: Write the mayor's {{count}} FICTIF parcels in {{repo}} and put them on the board.
summary.label: Put the label "{{label}}" on issue #{{issueNumber}}.
summary.duplicate: Close issue #{{issueNumber}} as a duplicate of #{{original}}.
summary.checklist: Add a Definition of Ready of {{items}} lines under issue #{{issueNumber}}.
summary.sprint-field: Start a one-week sprint on the board of {{repo}}, from today.
summary.load: Load issue #{{issueNumber}} on this week's sprint.
summary.milestone: Create the milestone "{{title}}" in {{repo}}, due {{dueOn}}, and put {{count}} jobs under it.
summary.split: Cut issue #{{issueNumber}} into {{count}} FICTIF parts, each its own issue on the board.
summary.bulletin: Post the evening bulletin on the board of {{repo}}, status {{status}}.
summary.wip-limit: Write the limit {{limit}} on the zone Being laid of {{repo}}'s board.
summary.team-day: The team's day: start {{count}} jobs, moved to Being laid.
summary.finish: Close issue #{{issueNumber}} as done, and lay it in the last zone.
summary.close-visit: Close milestone {{milestone}}: the mayor's visit is ready.

sprint-field.title: Start a sprint
sprint-field.body: The game adds a Sprint field to your board: one week, from today. Then you load the truck with what the team can carry.

load.title: Load issue #{{number}} on the sprint
load.body: It goes on this week's sprint. Mind the capacity: only the game counts it, GitHub does not.

unload.title: Take issue #{{number}} off the sprint
unload.body: Too much on the truck? Take this one off; it waits for a later sprint.

milestone.title: Set the mayor's visit
milestone.body: A milestone is a date everyone sees, with the jobs that must be laid by then.

attach.title: Put issue #{{number}} under a milestone
attach.body: The mayor will see this one too on her visit.

split.title: Split issue #{{number}}
split.body: One part per line, at least two. Each becomes a FICTIF issue on the board, and a sub-issue of this one.

rope.title: Rope issue #{{number}}
rope.body: This one cannot start before the other is done: GitHub marks it blocked by it.

bulletin.title: The evening bulletin
bulletin.body: The site radio drafted it from your board. Say how the site stands tonight, then post it as the board's status.

wip-limit.open: Set the limit on Being laid
wip-limit.title: A limit on Being laid
wip-limit.body: How many jobs can be laid at once? The game writes the limit in that zone's description on GitHub, where everyone sees it.

team-day.title: The team's day
team-day.body: The fictitious team starts jobs, more than the limit allows. Each move is listed below before anything is sent. Then bring Being laid back under its limit.

finish.title: Finish issue #{{number}}
finish.body: The job is done: close it as completed and lay it in the last zone.

close-visit.title: The mayor's visit is ready
close-visit.body: Every job of her visit is done: close the milestone.

move-visit.title: Move the mayor's visit
move-visit.body: It won't be ready in time: move the date now, and say it in the bulletin.

commands.editReadme: change README.md in your editor, then:
commands.makeFix: make the fix in README.md, then:

warm.wordsHint: A few words of thanks, in your own voice
warm.noMention: The game adds no @mention: only the words you write are sent.
